2010.text: Assertion : Diabetes insipidus is marked by excessive urination and too much thirst of water. Reason : Anti-diuretic hormone (ADH) is secreted by the posterior lobe of pituitary gland.
options: If both assertion and reason are true and reason is the correct explanation of assertion
If both assertion and reason are true but reason is not the correct explanation of assertion
If assertion is true but reason is false
If both assertion and reason are false.
2010.sol: Antidiuretic hormone ( ADH ) or vasopressin is secreted from posterior pituitary gland. It is released in response to a fall in the water content of blood plasma and leads to an increase in the permeability to water of the distal and collecting tubules of the nephron. Deficiency or hyposecretion of ADH results in diabetes insipidus. Diabetes insipidus is characterised by micturating dilute urine several times a day which results in excessive thirst (polydipsia) and dehydration.

28384.sol: Enzyme inhibitors are molecules that interact with enzymes (temporary or permanent) in some way and reduce the rate of an enzyme-catalyzed reaction or prevent enzymes to work in a normal manner. 71454.text: Given below are two statements regarding anaerobic respiration in the muscles. Statement (I): In muscles, NADH+H ^+ produced during glycolysis is reoxidised to NAD. Both Statement (I) and Statement (II) are incorrect.
Statement (I) is correct but Statement (II) is incorrect.

71454.sol: Statement (I) is correct because during anaerobic respiration in muscle cells (lactic acid fermentation), the NADH + H ^+ produced during glycolysis is reoxidised to NAD ^+ to ensure a continuous supply of NAD ^+ for glycolysis to proceed. Statement (II) is incorrect because during the reduction of pyruvic acid to lactic acid, NADH + H ^+ donates two protons ( 2 H ^+ ) and two electrons ( 2 e ^- ) to pyruvic acid, not one proton and two electrons. 71573.subject: Biology
71573.text: According to the proton transport theory of stomatal mechanism, protons are formed in guard cells when ____.
options: starch is converted into sugar during night time
sugar is converted into starch during the day time.
Potassium malate is formed during the night time
Malic acid dissociates to form malate during day time
71573.sol: According to the active potassium ion transport theory (proton transport theory) proposed by Levitt, stomatal opening during the daytime is driven by the accumulation of potassium ions in the guard cells. During the daytime, starch in the guard cells is converted into malic acid. Malic acid then dissociates into malate anions and protons ( H^+ ). These protons are actively pumped out of the guard cells into the surrounding subsidiary cells, and in exchange, potassium ions ( K^+ ) are transported into the guard cell

80377.sol: The sporophyte is more developed in mosses rather than liverwort. The simplest sporophyte is found in Riccia, a liverwort, where it is represented by capsule only. 121390.sol: Lichens are symbiotic associations i.e. mutually useful associations, between algae and fungi. These structures serve as the sites of attachment of spindle fibres (formed by the spindle fibres) to the chromosomes that are moved into position at the centre of the cell. 126772.subject: Botany

126772.sol: Prosthetic groups are organic compounds that are tightly bound to the apoenzyme. 134872.text: Which of the following representations correctly shows the palindromic sequence and the exact cleavage sites (indicated by arrows) for the restriction endonuclease EcoRI?
options: 5' G A A T T C 3' 3' C T T A A G 5'
5' G A A T T C 3' 3' C T T A A G 5'
5' G A A T T C 3' 3' C T T A A G 5'
5' G A A T T C 3' 3' C T T A A G 5'
134872.sol: EcoRI recognizes the 6-base pair palindromic sequence 5' - G A A T T C - 3'. It does not cut exactly in the center of the palindrome (which would produce blunt ends). Instead, it cuts between the same two bases on the opposite strands, specifically between the G and A bases. This staggered cut generates overhanging stretches called sticky ends. Therefore, the correct cleavage site is between G and A on the 5' 3' strand, and between A and G on the 3' 5' strand. Answer: 5' G A A T T C 3' 3' C T T A A G 5'

6a1bb6c0107bf677676d9fa4.text: Given below are two statements: Statement I: Exchange of nutrients and gases between the blood and the cells always occurs through the interstitial fluid. Statement II: As blood passes through tissue capillaries, larger proteins and most of the formed elements move out into the intercellular spaces to form tissue fluid. In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given be
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
6a1bb6c0107bf677676d9fa4.sol: As blood passes through the capillaries in tissues, water along with many small water-soluble substances move out into the spaces between the cells of tissues, leaving the larger proteins and most of the formed elements in the blood vessels. This fluid released out is called the interstitial fluid or tissue fluid. Therefore, Statement II is incorrect because larger proteins and formed elements do not move out into the intercellular spaces. The interstitial fluid has the same mineral distribution as that in plasma.

96036.sol: Endoplasmic reticulum is a network of tubular structures present in the cytoplasm which divide the intracellular space into luminal and extra luminal. These ER can be divided into two types depending upon the presence of ribosome on their outer surface. The rough endoplasmic reticulum (RER) has ribosomes on the outer surface while the smooth endoplasmic reticulum (SER) lacks presence of ribosomes. RER is involved in protein synthesis and secretion where as SER is involved in synthesis of lipids and lipid like hormo

96319.subject: Botany
96319.text: In animal and plant cell the division of cytoplasm is respectively
96319.sol: In animal cell cytokinesis occurs by cell furrow or groove formation in which a furrow develops in membrane which gradually grows towards the center thus shows centripetal growth. In plant cell cytokinesis occurs by cell plate which gradually grows from center to periphery thus shows centrifugal growth.

96551.text: The sudden mass killing of fishes is likely to be seen in a
96551.sol: Organic pollutants provide nutrients for stimulating the growth of algae and other plants. Algal bloom reduces the availability of light to submerged plants consumes more oxygen in decomposition. This reduces the availability of oxygen to other life forms leading to death of organisms. This is known as eutrophication.

96638.sol: Standing crop - It represents the quantity of biomass in an ecosystem. The whole living matter is represented by it and it is not circulated. There are continuous consumption and synthesis of biomass. Standing state - The total quantity of inorganic nutrients in an ecosystem is represented as a standing state. The whole of the non-living matter is represented by it and there is circulation between the biotic and abiotic components of the ecosystem.

6a7a1ff89a79a99b97aa71d1.subject: Chemistry
6a7a1ff89a79a99b97aa71d1.text: Given below are four statements regarding the properties and trends of halogens and their oxides: (A) Chemical reactivity of an element can be determined by its reaction with oxygen and halogens. (B) The stability of oxides of halogens follows the decreasing order Cl > Br > I . (C) Chlorine oxides are highly reactive oxidizing agents and tend to explode. (D) Lower oxides of halogens are generally more stable than the
6a7a1ff89a79a99b97aa71d1.sol: Statement (A) is correct. Oxygen and halogens are highly electronegative and reactive, hence their reactions are used as benchmarks to determine the chemical reactivity of elements. Statement (B) is incorrect. The stability of halogen oxides follows the order I > Cl > Br . Iodine oxides are the most stable due to the greater polarizability of the iodine atom, while chlorine oxides are stabilized by multiple bond formation. Bromine oxides lack both characteristics and are the least stable. Statement (C) is correct.
